def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    remaining = bins - item
    valid = remaining >= 0
    priority_scores = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf)
    priority_scores[valid] = -remaining[valid]
    return priority_scores

algorithm: {We assign priority based on the relative utilization of each bin after adding the item, favoring bins that are closest to full without overflowing, while penalizing bins that are already nearly empty to encourage balanced distribution.}

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    remaining = bins - item
    valid = remaining >= 0
    utilization = (bins - remaining) / bins if (bins != 0).any() else np.zeros_like(bins)
    utilization[~valid] = 0
    priority_scores = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf)
    priority_scores[valid] = utilization[valid]
    return priority_scores

algorithm: {We assign priority based on the relative utilization of each bin after adding the item, favoring bins that are closest to half-full to balance load distribution, while penalizing bins that would overflow or remain significantly underutilized.}

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    remaining = bins - item
    valid = remaining >= 0
    utilization = (bins - remaining) / bins
    target_utilization = 0.5
    deviation = np.abs(utilization - target_utilization)
    priority_scores = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf)
    priority_scores[valid] = -deviation[valid]
    return priority_scores

algorithm: {We assign priority based on the inverse of the product of the current bin capacity and the remaining capacity after adding the item, favoring bins that are neither too full nor too empty, while penalizing overflow.}

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    remaining = bins - item
    valid = remaining >= 0
    priority_scores = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf)
    with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
        priority_scores[valid] = 1.0 / (bins[valid] * remaining[valid])
    return priority_scores

algorithm: {The algorithm prioritizes bins based on how close their current load is to the median load across all bins, rewarding bins that are near the median to promote uniformity and reduce variance in bin utilization.}
function:
def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    current_loads = bins
    median_load = np.median(current_loads)
    deviations = np.abs(current_loads - median_load)
    remaining_capacity = bins - item
    valid = remaining_capacity >= 0
    priority_scores = np.full_like(bins, -np.inf)
    priority_scores[valid] = 1 / (deviations[valid] + 1e-8)
    return priority_scores
